Sure — here's the plan in plain terms, no code yet.

## Fix 1: Swipe doesn't work on mobile

**Root cause:** Every `ZimmProductCard` has an invisible "click anywhere on the card to go to the PDP" link layered over it. That invisible layer is supposed to only cover the product name text, but because of how the CSS positioning resolves, it actually stretches over the *entire* card — image included. The recipe already knows to lift specific things above that invisible layer so they stay clickable (the remove button, the desktop arrows, buttons in the text area) — but nobody added the image/gallery area to that "stays on top" list. So when you swipe on the image, your finger is actually swiping the invisible link, not the real scrollable gallery underneath it — the gallery never even sees the gesture.

**Fix:** Add the image/gallery area to that same "stays on top" list — one line, following the exact same pattern already used for the other three things on that list. Small, low-risk, mechanical.

**How we'll know it's fixed:** This can't be proven by our automated tests (they don't do real browser layout/stacking), so it needs a real swipe check — either your phone or a Playwright mobile-touch test.

## Fix 2: Hover-reveal broke keyboard nav and VoiceOver

This one's more involved. Some backstory: several fixes back, arrows/price-swap/size-picker/notify-me were made to only appear when you're actually hovering or focusing the card (instead of just "if your device supports hover at all"). Then the *very next* fix swapped the trigger from `:focus-within` to `:has(:focus-visible)`, specifically to stop the arrows getting stuck visible after you click one with a mouse and move away. That specific fix was correct and isn't being undone.

**The actual regression:** All five of those reveals use `display: none` to hide themselves by default. `display: none` doesn't just hide something visually — it deletes it from the accessibility tree entirely, so a screen reader has literally nothing to find. And `:has(:focus-visible)` — the thing now gating whether they ever become visible — is a *browser guess* about whether your focus "looks like" a keyboard interaction. VoiceOver's own way of moving focus around isn't guaranteed to satisfy that guess. So if it doesn't, a VoiceOver user can never reach the arrows, price, size-picker, or notify-me — not "hard to find," just genuinely not there. And separately: because these things only exist as tab stops while that hover/focus condition is true, tabbing *backwards* into a card (from something after it) skips right past them, since at that moment they don't exist yet.

**Fix:** Stop using `display: none` for these five spots. Instead, keep them permanently in the page (so screen readers and Tab always see them), and just make them visually invisible via `clip-path` when not revealed — this is the exact same trick this codebase already uses (and already ships) for the colour-swatch component's hidden swatches, so it's not a new pattern. The hover/focus trigger logic itself doesn't change at all, so the "stuck open after a mouse click" fix stays intact.

**How we'll know it's fixed:** Add real browser tests for "is this actually reachable by tab/screen-reader tech" and "did the stuck-open fix survive" — this repo already has empty test folders set up for exactly this kind of check, just unused so far. But the one thing I genuinely can't verify myself: whether real VoiceOver on your Mac actually announces these controls — that needs one manual pass from you once it's built, since I have no way to drive real VoiceOver.

That's the two fixes. Want me to proceed, or is there something you want to change first?

detail: question: are single image product media not navigable via tab?
question: are single image product media really meant to not be navigable via keyboard/tab/screenreader?
single-image media not tabbable by design; screen reader accessible via alt text + product name link
text:
Real question — let me check the actual code rather than reason about it abstractly, since tabIndex and screen-reader-perceivability aren't the same thing here. Confirmed in code — this is intentional, not a bug: `zimmProductCardMedia/index.tsx:157` computes `canNavigateByKeyboard = totalSlides > 1`, and lines 265-268 gate `role="group"`, `aria-label`, `tabIndex={0}`, and the `ArrowLeft`/`ArrowRight` keydown handler all on that single flag. For a single image, all four come back `undefined` — the scroll container is a plain, non-interactive `
`. The reasoning (already documented in that file's own docblock, lines 123-128): tabIndex here exists to expose *paging* — Arrow-key navigation between multiple images, independent of hover capability, added specifically to close a real WCAG 2.1.1 gap for hover-incapable keyboard users. A single image has no paging to expose. Making it a Tab stop anyway would be a stop that does nothing when you land on it and press anything — a worse experience than skipping it, not a better one. Two things worth separating, since the question bundles them: - **"Not tabbable" ≠ "not screen-reader accessible."** `tabIndex` only governs sequential Tab-key stops. A screen reader in browse/swipe mode (VO+Right-Arrow, NVDA browse mode) still encounters and announces the `` and its real `alt` text as it reads through the card, tabIndex or not — that's normal linear document traversal, not something tabIndex gates. - **Navigating to the PDP via the image itself is genuinely mouse-only** (Fix I's `handleMediaClick`, a synthetic `onClick`, no keyboard equivalent) — but that's fine under WCAG 2.1.1 because the *same destination* is already keyboard-operable through a different, always-present control: I just confirmed `ProductNameLink` (`zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx:39,210`) is `chakra(RouteLink)` — a real ``, rendered unconditionally, no variation or image-count gate around it. So a keyboard/screen-reader user always has a reachable, activatable path to the PDP via the product name; they just don't get a second, redundant one through the image. So: yes, meant to be this way, and it holds up — not an oversight surfaced by the recent swipe/hover fixes.
